privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: What JobFinder stores, what it sends to other services, and how to remove it, in plain words. This page describes what the app does. It is not a legal contract.

store.title: What we store
store.account: Your account: your name, your email address, and a one-way hash of your password. The password itself is never stored.
store.google: If you continue with Google, we receive your name, email address and Google account id. Signing in with Google never reads your Gmail.
store.content: What you make in the app: your resumes and their earlier versions, tailored drafts, the applications in your tracker, the job searches you run, your job alerts and any feedback you send.
store.usage: How much you used the app each day and each month, so the limits work. The monthly count is kept when you delete your data or close your account, under a one-way code made from your email address, and deleted within two months. Whether you have had your free first search is kept under that same code and not deleted, so it stays one per address.
store.steps: The first time you reach a few steps (uploading a resume, a search, a tailor, a download, saving a job, coming back within a week), with the date and nothing else, so we can tell whether the app works for new people. Deleting your data deletes them.
store.push: If you turn on notifications on a device, we keep that device's notification address, and your browser's push service (Google, Apple, Mozilla or Microsoft) delivers them, encrypted so it cannot read them. Turning them off or deleting your data deletes the address.
store.whatsapp: If you turn on WhatsApp alerts, we keep your phone number and send it, with each alert, to WhatsApp (Meta), which delivers the message. Removing the number, deleting your data or closing your account deletes it.
store.security: A sign-in security log: sign-ins, failed attempts, code requests and password changes. Each sign-in keeps the device type and a coarse network hint, which are removed 30 days after that session ends.

gmail.title: If you connect Gmail
gmail.optional: Connecting Gmail is optional, and the access is read-only. JobFinder cannot send, delete or change your mail.
gmail.reads: It looks for replies to your job applications (confirmations, interview invitations, rejections and offers) and uses them to fill in your tracker.
gmail.keeps: For each job email it recognises, it keeps the sender, the date, the subject, a short preview, what kind of reply it is, the company and role, and a short quote that shows why. Full emails are never stored.
gmail.skips: Job-alert digests and mail that is clearly not about an application are skipped by fixed rules before any AI sees them. Other emails that might be about a job are read by an AI model (OpenAI) to decide. We keep only the job details we detect and a short preview, never the full email.
gmail.token: The access Google grants is stored encrypted and is never sent to your browser.
gmail.limitedUseBefore: JobFinder's use and transfer of information received from Google APIs to any other app will adhere to the
gmail.policyLink: Google API Services User Data Policy

ai.title: AI processing
ai.tools: Tailoring, interview practice and the other AI tools send the resume and job text you give them to OpenAI to produce the result. The resume scan is the exception: it is scored in our own code and reaches no AI service.
ai.mail: With Gmail connected, an email the fixed rules cannot sort is sent to OpenAI on its own, to read the company, the role and the kind of reply.

extension.title: If you use the Chrome extension
extension.reads: The JobFinder Job Clipper extension reads a page only when you click its icon, and only the tab you clicked it on: the job's title, company, description and link (or the page's visible text, where it finds no description). It shows them to you first, and none of it is sent until you press Save to tracker or Save & tailor.
extension.sends: It talks only to the JobFinder server set in its options, which is this site unless you change it, and signs in with your extension key. When it opens, it also loads your saved jobs and application kits from your account, to tell you if this job is already saved and to list your approved kits.
extension.fill: When you press Autofill this page, it fills the application form on that tab with your own details from the approved kit you choose: name, email, phone, location, LinkedIn and website links, the resume file and the cover letter. It does not overwrite text you typed, and it never submits the form. You check it and send it yourself.
extension.ai: Open questions on that form, up to four each time, are sent to JobFinder with the kit's resume and job description. JobFinder's AI drafts the answers through OpenAI, like the other AI tools.
extension.stores: It keeps only its options, your extension key among them, in Chrome's sync storage, which Chrome copies to your other devices when Chrome sync is on. It keeps no copy of the pages it reads or the jobs you save.
extension.none: It has no analytics or tracking and shows no ads, and nothing it reads is sold.
extension.remove: To remove it, open chrome://extensions and click Remove on its card. That deletes its options and your key from Chrome. The jobs it saved stay in your account until you delete them (below). To switch off a copy you no longer control, replace the browser extension key in Settings: the old key stops working at once.
extension.limitedUse: The extension's use of this information adheres to the Chrome Web Store User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.

remove.title: Removing your data
remove.wipe: In Settings, "Delete all my data" removes everything you made and keeps your account.
remove.close: In Settings, "Close my account" removes the same data, deletes your sign-in details and signs you out on every device. Security-log entries are unlinked from the account and expire within 30 days. This month's use count stays until it expires.
